mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during periods when UNRATE > 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and increases risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 6-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months signals improved labor supply, which supports higher consumer demand and corporate output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS above 12-month MA for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is stable and PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months.
